transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net priority broadband support. My name is Will. How may I direct your call?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Will, listen to me very carefully! My entire gigabit fiber internet has collapsed right in the middle of the US market opening bell! I have over eighty thousand pounds of open leveraged futures contracts on the Chicago Mercantile Exchange hanging without stop-loss protection! Every single second your connection stays down I am hemorrhaging hundreds of pounds! Fix this immediately!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I understand how critical and urgent this financial trading session is, Dylan. Let's look into your optical connection status immediately to restore your service.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you Will, but you don't understand, I am watching my margin call liquidation threshold approach on my mobile phone screen right now!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Before we access the optical line telemetry, could you please verify your installation address and your four-digit security PIN?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The installation address is 17 St. Andrew's Crescent, Cardiff, CF10 3DD, and the security PIN is 8841. My trader gateway static IP subnet is 194.72.10.0.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for verifying those details, Dylan. I have your Cardiff fiber terminal open on our diagnostics screen.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Great, what does the line test say?!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: So just to confirm the emergency situation: your fiber connection dropped abruptly during the opening of the financial markets, threatening active trading positions, and you require immediate restoration. Is that correct?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, exactly! I need the packets flowing right this second or our trading accounts will be completely wiped out!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Please bear with me on hold for about forty-five seconds while I query the local optical distribution node on Queen Street.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for holding, Dylan. The Queen Street optical line card experienced an automated circuit breaker trip following a sudden power surge.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: A power surge?! Why on earth doesn't S-Net have redundant backup battery supplies in your exchange racks?!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The secondary uninterruptible power supply engaged immediately, but the optical line termination blade required an automated firmware restart cycle.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: How long does this ridiculous restart take?! I am down four thousand pounds already while we talk!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The optical blade boot cycle takes between three and five minutes to re-establish optical framing with all downstream subscriber ONTs.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Three to five minutes?! Are you completely insane?! Three minutes will wipe out my entire trading account! Do something manually right now!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Dylan, screaming over the telephone line will not accelerate the physical boot sequence of an optical line card.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Don't you dare tell me not to scream! You work for a third-rate cowboy ISP that is costing me thousands! You are completely incompetent!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Just shut up Dylan and listen to me! Screaming abuse in my ear won't bring your fiber connection back any faster, so stop interrupting and let me explain what the exchange logs show!

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Did you just tell me to shut up?! How dare you tell a paying customer to shut up! I will have you fired by the end of today!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I apologize for losing my temper, Dylan. However, verbally abusing support representatives is unacceptable under our customer conduct policy.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I am losing my life savings and you expect polite conversation?!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The optical line card has completed its POST self-test and the downstream lasers are actively relocking with subscriber terminals across Cardiff.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Wait... the optical light on my wall box just turned solid green.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, the optical PON link is restored and your IP gateway session is re-established with your static IP subnet, routing packets directly through our Cardiff core switch without dropped frames.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Let me check my trading terminal... the live candlestick charts are updating again, and orders are executing on the order book.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am glad to confirm that your primary gigabit trading throughput is fully operational.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I managed to close the riskiest Nasdaq options contracts just in time before automated broker liquidation took place.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Just to confirm what you mentioned earlier, the registered trader gateway static IP subnet on your account is 194.72.10.0?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, 194.72.10.0 is our registered static subnet for all our fixed trading terminals and server connections.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Are all of your trading monitors connected via hardwired Cat6 Ethernet cabling directly into your gigabit switch?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, all our high-frequency screens are wired directly into a managed Cisco switch on port 1.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Does the switch front panel show full duplex gigabit link negotiation on that uplink port?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, the LED is solid green indicating one gigabit full duplex with zero transmission collisions.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: To ensure redundancy during market hours, does your trading terminal feature automated dual-WAN failover capability?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: We have a secondary 4G backup router, but the automatic failover gateway was misconfigured to wait five minutes before switching over.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Configuring the failover threshold to ten seconds will provide seamless continuity in the event of any future carrier line glitches.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: How should we adjust the health-check ICMP ping frequency on that dual-WAN failover router?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Set the ICMP echo probes to ping 1.1.1.1 and 8.8.8.8 every two seconds, with a three-packet failure trigger to initiate cellular failover within six seconds.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That will make failover instantaneous if the primary optical circuit ever hiccups in future.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I also recommend setting static DNS servers to 1.1.1.1 and 8.8.8.8 on the primary network interface to prevent local resolver cache misses during failover transition.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I will configure those primary and secondary DNS resolvers across all our trading terminals.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That ensures that host resolution for the Chicago Mercantile Exchange gateway continues seamlessly across both optical and 4G links.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I will have our network administrator verify that routing table and failover configuration this evening.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: To compensate for the severe stress and disruption during today's market session, I have applied a thirty-pound goodwill credit to your broadband billing invoice.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thirty pounds doesn't cover market slippage, but I appreciate the gesture.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The exchange incident ticket logged by network operations is INC-77401-C.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Noted down... INC-77401-C.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The Cardiff exchange engineering supervisor has confirmed that redundant power regulation on that rack has been permanently upgraded with surge arrestors.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That will give us much more peace of mind during future morning trading sessions.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: How is your S-Net mobile phone network coverage performing when you are out of the office in Cardiff?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Our mobile phone network with S-Net has always had excellent 5G signal across Cardiff and the Bay area, we get fast data everywhere, so mobile service is great.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: We are pleased that your commercial 5G cellular coverage maintains reliable performance across South Wales.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, mobile has been completely solid.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The thirty-pound account credit and line stabilization are confirmed on your profile.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you Will, despite the heated moment earlier, thank you for getting the connection back up quickly.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have verified that your gigabit fiber line is fully synchronized, the Queen Street exchange card is operating normally, and the thirty-pound goodwill credit is applied. Does that address all of your concerns regarding the outage today, Dylan?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes Will, you've resolved the line and answered everything. Thank you.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for choosing S-Net today. Have a productive afternoon. Goodbye Dylan.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you Will, goodbye.
